newsitem.title: GERMANY: German weather channel to boost local reports.
newsitem.headline: German weather channel to boost local reports.

text.p: German private TV station Wetter Kanal (Weather Channel) said on Wednesday it planned to offer local forecasts for 100 cities and regions by the end of the year, up from the current total of 19.

A study by market research firms IRES and Emnid showed that 1.9 million viewers watch the channel at least once a day and Christian Boehmer, chief executive of Wetter und Reise Television GmbH & Co. KG. said the station hoped to boost ratings with more region-specific reports.
"We want to offer viewers the closest thing to weather on demand day and night," Boehmer told Reuters at the two-day German TV ad fair. "Above all, viewers want to see local weather reports."

He added that Germans are more interested in tracking the weather than viewers in the United States and that the station was even considering introducing special forecasts for soccer fans before matches.
Boehmer said the channel anticipated about 10 million marks in turnover for the year but was wary of competition for up-to-the-minute weather updates from multimedia services.
The station has been available since June 1996 on cable services.

Investors include the U.S.-based Weather Channel with 45 percent of the shares, publishing group Holtzbrinck/Mairs, Deutsche Fernsehnachrichten Agentur, Gesellschaft fuer Telekommunikation and Klausnitzer GmbH.
